item.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $\alpha$, LP-$\alpha$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$\alpha$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $\xi$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $\xi$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $\phi$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $\phi$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $\alpha$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $\xi$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $\phi$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $\xi$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.
item.dc:creator: Absos Ali Shaikh

item.title: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.
item.dc:creator: Junzhang Li

item.title: Calibrations close to $\mathrm{G}_2$-twistor space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.
item.dc:creator: Rui Albuquerque

item.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients. Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls. For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoshang Jin

item.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.29017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Dittmer

item.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Satyajit Guin, Pradip Kumar

item.title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.29268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. For a non-uniruled compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ satisfying $\mu_{\omega_0,\max}(T_X)=0$ for some Gauduchon metric $\omega_0$, we show that the corresponding maximal destabilizing subsheaf of $T_X$ splits off holomorphically and is polystable of slope zero with respect to every Gauduchon metric. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact K\"ahler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $\omega$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $\omega$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $\kappa^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Chuanjing Zhang, Xi Zhang

item.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
item.description: arXiv:2610.29360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Shiobara

item.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.29444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.
item.dc:creator: Xianfeng Jiang

item.title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions $2\le n\le 5$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $\mu$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.
item.dc:creator: Chenghang Lu

item.title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
item.description: arXiv:2610.29579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B(\delta)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<\delta<\pi/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,\alpha}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cot\delta$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Liuwei Gong, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.29596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g \le 2n(n-1)\omega_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le16\pi r, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$. Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le12\pi(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le\bigl[8\pi(1-v)+200\pi(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8\pi$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.
item.dc:creator: Qixuan Hu

item.title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
item.description: arXiv:2610.29769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $\pi:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.
item.dc:creator: Mingwei Zhang

item.title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.29796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2\pi$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.
item.dc:creator: Bin Shen, Hui Zhang

item.title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2610.29842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Li, Guoxin Wei, Cheng Xing

item.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ \Gamma=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Sheng, Ye Zhu

item.title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Chun-Pong Chu, Daniel Stern

item.title: On complete Ricci--flat K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.29891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat K\"ahler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat K\"ahler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no K\"ahler compactification.
item.dc:creator: Song Sun, Junsheng Zhang

item.title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.30130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized K\"ahler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to K\"ahler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $\nu$-soliton equation in K\"ahler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.
item.dc:creator: Beatrice Brienza

item.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexander B. Goncharov, Zhe Sun

item.title: Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.28894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. We discuss some rigidity consequences, as well as an extension to the higher-order GJMS operators.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Eddaoudi

item.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schr\"odinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.29514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties. Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure. With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Bisterzo, Salvatore Lincastri, Giona Veronelli

item.title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2\pi$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11\pi^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Roger Z\"ust

item.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
item.description: arXiv:2610.29704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.
item.dc:creator: Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi, Giorgio Saracco

item.title: On electrostatic manifolds with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2505.05581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Static manifolds with boundary were recently introduced in the context of the problem of prescribing both the scalar curvature of a Riemannian manifold and the mean curvature of its boundary. These manifolds are also of interest from the perspective of general relativity. In this article, we introduce electrostatic manifolds with boundary as a natural generalization of static manifolds with boundary in the presence of a nonzero electric field. We also introduce Robin electrostatic quadruples, extending the notion of Robin static triples previously introduced by the second author. We establish several uniqueness theorems for suitable regions of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om manifold. Finally, we characterize the criticality of the first eigenvalue of an associated mixed Robin-Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operator under admissible volume-preserving variations in terms of the equality of the surface gravities along the Dirichlet boundary components.
item.dc:creator: Stanislav Demurov, Vladimir Medvedev

item.title: Non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics of two summands
item.description: arXiv:2505.06631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on a class of compact manifolds arising as double disk bundles, whose principal orbits split into two inequivalent irreducible summands. The proof uses a phase space barrier argument that yields a new obstruction to the existence of closed cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, even when the principal orbits admit homogeneous Einstein metrics.
item.dc:creator: Hanci Chi

item.title: $SU(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs functional with Higgs self-interaction on $3$-manifolds
item.description:

When $M$ is closed, we use a $3$-parameter min-max construction to produce, for $\varepsilon\ll_M 1$, non-trivial critical points in the energy regime \[ 1 \lesssim_{\lambda}\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal{Y}_{\varepsilon}(

item.dc:creator: Da Rong Cheng, Daniel Fadel, Luiz Lara

item.title: A Note on Zoll Manifolds with Entire Grauert Tubes
item.description: arXiv:2508.03352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute several algebraic indices of the algebraization of the tangent bundle of a Zoll manifold that admits an entire Grauert tube. As an application, we prove that any Zoll manifold of type $\mathbb{HP}^2$ with an entire Grauert tube is isometric to the canonical $\mathbb{HP}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Kyobeom Song

item.title: Entropy Rigidity for Maximal Representations
item.description: arXiv:2601.03585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset \mathsf{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ be a lattice and $\rho:\Gamma\to \mathsf{Sp}(2n,\mathbb{R})$ be a maximal representation. We show that $\rho$ satisfies a measurable $(1,1,2)-$hypertransversality condition. With this we define a measurable Gromov product and the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure associated to the unstable Jacobian introduced by Pozzetti, Sambarino and Wienhard. As a main application, we prove a strong entropy rigidity result for $\rho$.
item.dc:creator: Zhufeng Yao

item.title: Warped area-minimizing hypersurface and warped product metric
item.description: arXiv:2603.12549v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several metric splitting theorems under spectral Ricci curvature lower bounds have been established in recent years, yet the existing literature mostly yields only isometric direct product decompositions. In some parameter regimes, direct product splitting is even known to fail. In this paper, we study warped (weighted) area-minimizing hypersurfaces and use their variational properties to prove local warped product metric splitting under spectral Ricci curvature conditions. Given a smooth compact connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ with non vanishing homology $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb Z)$, satisfying our spectral Ricci lower bound, and with dimension $3\le n\le 5$, we consider a nontrivial homological warped area-minimizing hypersurface $\Sigma$ whose existence follows from classical geometric measure theory. By analyzing the first and second variations of the warped area functional together with a foliation argument, we show that $M$ locally decomposes as a warped product $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times_f \Sigma$, where the warping function is given by $f=u^{-1}$ for the positive weight function $u$ appearing in the spectral Ricci condition. Our work complements the existing splitting theory for spectral Ricci curvature: even in parameter ranges where product type splitting cannot hold, we still obtain local warped product rigidity via weighted minimal hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Yukai Sun

item.title: On spherical Milnor Classifying Spaces I: differential geometry
item.description: arXiv:2605.16369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compare the original product-subset diffeology on the Milnor join of Magnot--Watts with the locally finite final diffeology on a signed spherical model. The canonical squaring map from the spherical space to the Magnot--Watts join is smooth, whereas the positive square-root section is generally not; we also construct a different smooth injection from the locally finite simplicial model whose inverse is not smooth. For Hausdorff Fr\'echet--Lie groups whose smooth real-valued functions separate points, we compute the full algebraic internal tangent space, exhibiting separate first-order branches labelled by elements of the group at every inactive coordinate. The spherical weighted energy descends plotwise and restricts to a Riemannian metric on each support stratum. Smooth normalized strictly positive-definite kernels yield non-canonical ambient tangent metrics; compact Lie groups admit an explicit realization through their heat kernels. We characterize global diffeological forms by descent, construct plotwise Hausdorff Jacobians and varying-degree complementary forms, and show why these data do not define a canonical Hodge star across support changes. Stratumwise Hodge--Dirac operators remain available, but an explicit example obstructs their automatic gluing. We prove smooth contractibility of the total spherical space for any diffeological group, as well as equivariant uniqueness of maps to it. For any diffeological group we establish a classifying theorem for $D$-numerable principal bundles, without regularity hypotheses. For Lie groups we construct barycentric connections and their Chern--Weil forms, and distinguish sign local systems from gerbes. The hypotheses and proofs specify which conclusions are global, stratumwise, or conditional.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Magnot

item.title: Spherical Milnor Spaces II: Projective Quotients and Higher Topological Structures
item.description: arXiv:2605.16370v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study projective and semidirect quotients of the spherical Milnor construction and develop a step-by-step lifting obstruction from their explicit spherical local sections. The resulting transition functions produce a twisted Cech 2-cocycle for any specified compatible extension with abelian kernel. When the kernel is $U(1)$ and the sign acts by complex conjugation, taking logarithms yields a twisted Dixmier--Douady obstruction under stated sheaf hypotheses. We identify its projective-operator interpretation when an additional representation is supplied, without attempting a classification of K-theory twists. We also investigate descent of differential-geometric structures and, under restricted-operator hypotheses, Schwinger cocycles and lifting gerbes for loop groups.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Magnot

item.title: A conformal reduction for the X-ADM mass
item.description: arXiv:2607.03629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The X-ADM mass is a generalisation of the ADM mass for asymptotically flat manifolds, recently introduced by Mantegazza and Oronzio [arXiv:2602.11372], who proved a positive mass theorem for this quantity in dimension $3$ under a certain topological condition. In this article, we prove the X-positive mass theorem with rigidity in all dimensions $n\geq3$ without any topological restrictions. To this end, we first prove that the scalar curvature condition appearing in the X-positive mass theorem implies the metric is of positive Yamabe type. We then show that the X-ADM mass of the given metric is equal to the ADM mass of a scalar-flat representative in its conformal class plus a term that is explicitly non-negative. From this, the X-positive mass theorem follows from the standard positive mass theorem. As a corollary, we obtain the Riemannian mass--charge inequality of general relativity in all dimensions, which was previously only known for spin manifolds. Finally, we give a version of the X-positive mass theorem for a manifold with boundary.
item.dc:creator: Stephen McCormick

item.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.19452v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbf R^n$ be a set of dimension $2$ with an isolated singular point $0$, such that $E-\{0\}$ is an orientable $\mathcal C^2$ submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$ of dimension $2$, and hence a Riemann surface with the conformal structure induced by the ambient metric. We study the extension of its conformal structure across $0$, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. Denoting by $S(0,r)$ the sphere of radius $r$ centred at $0$, we call the singularity $0$ $\mathit{M\text{-}regular}$ if (i) the pair $(E-\{0\},\{0\})$ satisfies a Whitney condition (the radial direction becomes asymptotically tangent to $E-\{0\}$ at $0$) and (ii) the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ is bounded above by a linear function of $r$ for small $r$ ($\mathit{metric\ decay}$). The main result (1989) is that an $M$-regular singularity is $\mathit{conformally\ point\text{-}like}$, that is, a punctured neighbourhood of $0$ in $E$ is conformal to the punctured unit disc $\Delta^*$, so that the conformal structure extends across $0$. The proof uses the modulus of rings (extremal length), which generalizes the classical planar technique to $2$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Two classes of surfaces are shown to be conformally point-like: all surfaces of revolution generated by a single $C^1$ curve, and orientable subanalytic sets of dimension $2$ with isolated singularities, for which $M$-regularity is proven directly from Hironaka's structure theory. In this case the metric decay condition follows from a direct estimate of the volume of the slices $S(0,r)\cap E$ (Lemma 7.5), based on Hironaka's Whitney theorem and Stasica's decomposition into $L$-analytic pieces. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\mathit{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses defining $M$-regularity are independent.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: Hopf type theorem for surfaces of constant weighted mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.23036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider compact immersed surfaces of genus zero in a three-dimensional smooth metric measure space $(M^3,g,e^{-f}\mathrm{d}V_{g})$. We introduce a new weighted mean curvature and prove that any such surface whose weighted mean curvature is constant must be totally umbilical, provided that a condition relating the Ricci curvature of $M$ and the weight function $f$ is satisfied. We also give an application of this result to surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying $|x|^{2} H + 2\langle x,\nu \rangle = c$.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Chen, Shanze Gao

item.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
item.description: arXiv:2609.19464v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--\'Emery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.
item.dc:creator: Shunzi Guo

item.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.23822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.
item.dc:creator: Kyobeom Song

item.title: Biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with constant Gaussian curvature in $2$-dimensional complex space forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.05703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Constant curvature is one of the most fundamental intrinsic conditions in submanifold geometry. Investigating the existence and classification of biharmonic submanifolds under intrinsic curvature constraints is generally difficult, since the biharmonic equation is expressed in terms of extrinsic data. In this paper, we obtain a complete classification of proper, that is non-minimal, biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with constant Gaussian curvature in 2-dimensional complex space forms. As a consequence, we classify the proper biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with flat normal bundle and prove that pseudo-umbilical biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces are necessarily minimal.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu, Yanru Luo, Cezar Oniciuc

item.title: Mixed Chern curvature on complete flags
item.description: arXiv:2610.25864v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.
item.dc:creator: Yuqin Guo, Dongmei Zhang

item.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2411.06497v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.
item.dc:creator: Mathew George
